claims.statement: `assignChecked(target, name, value)` is the single patch primitive: it assigns inside try/catch (returning false instead of throwing on a non-writable target), then reads the property back and compares by identity, so a write swallowed by an Xray expando is detected; it never logs — callers decide what a false return means.

CommonJS modules obtained via require() run in their own sandbox with frozen exports and are therefore excluded as patch targets; this exclusion is documented as part of the silent-patch-failure pitfall and anchored in docs/anchors.md.

Every patch site follows the same lifecycle: feature-detect the target and member before wrapping, hold the native function in module state together with the target, apply the wrapper through assignChecked and log a false result, then restore the original through assignChecked in stop/unpatch — the original is kept in module state or closure, never re-read from the target, and citeOnly clears its installed state upon restore so concurrent calls cannot enter a corrupted state.

Patch failure semantics differ by design: citeOnlyPatch.start() throws when the _insertCitingResult patch did not take effect (the feature registry logs the error without aborting other features), while persistentDialogPatch.start() rolls back — if displayDialog, execCommand, or Interface methods could not be patched it unpatches them, sets alive=false and returns without error.

Patches are idempotent: an installed patch returns early on a second call, and CitaviImport.patch() explicitly refuses to wrap translate twice so a later unpatch() peels exactly one layer; the Zotero tests pin no-double-patch and full restore for both citeOnly and Citavi.

The core monkey-patched Zotero symbols include Zotero.Integration.Session.prototype._insertCitingResult, Zotero.Translate.Import.prototype.translate, the per-window Zotero_File_Interface.importFile/importFromClipboard, Zotero.Reader.open, Zotero.Integration.displayDialog, Zotero.Integration.Progress.prototype.show, Zotero.Integration.execCommand, Zotero.Integration.Interface.prototype.addEditCitation/addAnnotation, and AnnotationRow.prototype.render — all applied via assignChecked and restored in stop or removeFromWindow, while reader menus use official event listeners and dialog layouts use DOM injection.

The patched _insertCitingResult implements citation-only insertion: with the citationOnly pref on it rewrites a citation of annotations into a citation of the parent items (annotationPageLabel as locator) and calls _insertItemsIntoDocument itself; any other case or any error falls through to the native method, so the insertion never fails because of the patch.

The Citavi pass has two entrypoints with distinct roles: the Translate.Import.translate wrapper decides what runs (it detects a Citavi export by translator label and parks the translation object as pending), while the per-window importFile/importFromClipboard wrappers decide when it runs (they trigger the pass in their finally, after Zotero's own annotation pass — required because Zotero takes getAttachments()[0] and a placeholder created earlier could otherwise receive the PDF annotations).

Zotero_File_Interface is not a singleton — every window that loads fileInterface.js gets its own object, and the import wizard loads the script itself — so patching only the main window silently misses other windows and the wizard; therefore CitaviImport patches importFile/importFromClipboard on each window's own object, records them in a windowPatches WeakMap keyed by window, restores them in removeFromWindow, and patches newly opened windows via a Services.ww domwindowopened observer on their load event.

The Citavi sequencing state uses a Set<Window> (sequencedWindows) instead of a module-level boolean so the state clears when the last sequenced window closes; without any sequenced window the pass runs right after translate() and the code logs that PDF annotations of the same sources could then land on the placeholder, and _afterTranslate logs when a queued pass was never triggered because the import's call path bypassed every patched window object.

Per-window and per-instance bookkeeping lives in WeakMaps/WeakSets keyed by the window or reader instance — never on module objects, which exist once per session while windows come and go: liveRects (WeakMap<Window, Rect>) and browseWindows (WeakSet<Window>) in the persistent-dialog patch, watchedReaders (WeakSet<ReaderInstance>) in readerMenu; this is the repo-wide convention from pitfall 11 and AGENTS.md.

The persistent-dialog patches have distinct behaviors: the displayDialog wrapper opens the citation dialog window itself and keeps Zotero.Integration.currentWindow set so execCommand's finally closes it; the Progress.prototype.show wrapper suppresses the orphan progress window when no integration transaction is running (no currentDoc); the execCommand wrapper records the last command (agent, docId, templateVersion) for persistent agents so the browse window can repeat it.

readerMenu wraps Zotero.Reader.open (assignChecked, original kept in module state origOpen) so every newly opened reader is watched and gets the page-number-popup enhancement via a MutationObserver on its iframe document; unpatch restores the original open and disconnects the observers.

Teardown is symmetric: onShutdown runs stopAll over the feature array in reverse order, restoring every patch through assignChecked, and a failed restore is logged rather than silent (citeOnly logs 'restore ... did not take effect'); per-window patches are restored earlier by removeFromWindow on window unload.

The patch lifecycle is pinned by Zotero integration tests reached through addon.api (never direct module imports, because feature modules need the ztoolkit global): the citeOnly start/second-start/stop round-trip against the real prototype, the Citavi translate double-start and window-file-interface restore, persistentDialogPatch stop() restoring both displayDialog and Progress.prototype.show with a later start() patching both again, and the reader patch/unpatch verified against Zotero's own listener registry.

The repo convention requires every patch to carry evidence — a test or a source anchor in docs/anchors.md; AGENTS.md states the assignChecked rule (check target, read back, log failure, restore in stop/removeFromWindow) and the evidence requirement, and docs/anchors.md records the patched symbols and their restore path.

citationDialog.ts implements a centralized CitationDialogWatcher that uses Services.wm to detect citationDialog.xhtml windows, polls DIALOG_STATE.loaded (up to 150 times at 200 ms intervals), executes registered DialogInjectors sequentially inside isolated try/catch blocks so errors never halt other injectors, and automatically invokes detach on window unload or feature stop.

The citation dialog is extended without prototype monkey-patching: modeSelector injects citation mode dropdowns into popups and follows mode switches via a MutationObserver on dialog-type, while outlineView introduces an outline browsing layout and initiates insertions by programmatically clicking the plus button of a hidden native <annotation-row>, keeping Zotero's internal citation pipeline and Word communication unmodified.

To prevent data corruption and process locks, patches and tests strictly avoid mutating production databases or unmanaged Word instances: runtime code uses Zotero's XPCOM APIs (saveTx, Zotero.Integration) with automatic fallback to native methods on errors, while automated tests run in isolated profiles (.scaffold/test/profile/), target only test-profile processes during process termination, and test dialog workflows via synthetic CitationEditInterface objects without invoking external Word documents.

AnnotationRow.prototype.render is patched via assignChecked to customize the annotation title with the resolved FlexAnnotate locator (such as margin numbers or opus) instead of Zotero's hardcoded page label, tracked per window in a WeakMap, applied to newly opened windows via addToWindow and citation dialogs via CitationDialogWatcher, and restored on window unload or feature teardown.

The persistent companion window intercepts Zotero.Integration.Interface.prototype methods addEditCitation and addAnnotation via assignChecked, immediately resolving Word transactions and opening the companion window when not inside an existing citation, which prevents empty footnote placeholders from being created in the host document.

citeOnlyPatch optionally patches Session.prototype.resetRequest via assignChecked to preserve the rebuildCiteprocState flag during session resets, preventing crashes in processCitationCluster when citations already exist in the document.
